messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Issue with gl2fasta after gl.join
messages.body_plain:
Hi Evgenii,

Yes, there is a bug. The workaround would be to assign the position and chromosome again after joining the datasets as in the code below. I tested the code below using the beta version of dartR, which can be installed as shown below.

This bug will be fixed in the next release of dartR.

# installing beta version of dartR
devtools::install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR@beta")
# restart your R session
library(dartR)
# test dataset
test_1 <- platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>
# assigning chromosome and position to genlight object 1
position(test_1) <- test_1$other$loc.metrics$ChromPos_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
chromosome(test_1) <- test_1$other$loc.metrics$Chrom_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
test_2 <- platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>
# assigning chromosome and position to genlight object 2
position(test_2) <- test_2$other$loc.metrics$ChromPos_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
chromosome(test_2) <- test_2$other$loc.metrics$Chrom_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
# joining datasets
test_join <- gl.join(test_1,test_2)
# assigning chromosome and position to joined genlight object
position(test_join) <- test_join$other$loc.metrics$ChromPos_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
chromosome(test_join) <- test_join$other$loc.metrics$Chrom_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1
# converting to fasta
test_fasta <- gl2fasta(test_join)

Cheers,
Luis

messages.body_plain:
Hi Laia,

I still could not figure out where you got the error from the information you sent.

There are different methods to perform AMOVA; dartR uses the AMOVA implementation from package pegas. I think you are trying to perform AMOVA using the method implemented in the package poppr. If you get the error from poppr, I suggest contacting poppr developers.

I suggest reading the documentation of the different AMOVA functions carefully. You can access the documentation of the functions, for example, by typing in the R console:

?poppr::poppr.AMOVA
?dartR::gl.AMOVA
?pegas::AMOVA
?StAMPP::stamppAMOVA

Here is how you can perform AMOVA in dartR and in poppr

library(dartR)
library(poppr)

# Here is AMOVA using dartR
# Don't use gl as a variable because it is a function in base R
gl_test <- bandicoot.gl <http://bandicoot.gl>
# Performing AMOVA
amova_dartr <- gl.amova(gl_test)

# Here is AMOVA using poppr
# Converting genlight to genind
geni <- gl2gi(gl_test)
# Assign pop information to strata
strata(geni) <- data.frame(pop = pop(geni))
# Performing AMOVA
amova_poppr <- poppr.amova(geni,~pop,nperm = 100)

Cheers,
Luis

Thanks,
Peter

Bernd

I have found the issue, and it is entirely self inflicted.
It appears that as the scripts were initially developed with an older version of dartR before gl.filter.maf was included. The function was later added when it became available but sourced locally. I've disabled this now and it appears to be running smoothly.
My apologies for this oversight on my part. Thank you for all of your support.

Kindest regards,
Adam
